contrary_evidence: Chinese iron-ore imports and crude-steel output are not directly comparable measures: ore grades, domestic ore, stock changes and shipment timing affect the relationship.
SteelHome port inventories are an industry survey, not a complete official inventory census; trader-held stocks are estimates.
Worldsteel's latest complete global comparison at the cutoff is September; October global production was not yet released.

The IEA reports a recovery in global crude supply and a 52-million-barrel increase in observed stocks in October, even while on-land stocks remained at their lowest level since at least 2016 and diesel stayed above pre-war levels.
SimFer progress and shipment figures are company-reported; construction milestones do not establish full operational capacity or stable nameplate throughput.
Brazil's October iron-ore export value fell more sharply than volume; the implied unit-value change is a derived measure, not a quoted benchmark price.
limitations: The SteelHome inventory survey is not a complete official census and trader-held inventory is estimated.
The iron-ore import and steel-output series use different definitions and cannot establish a direct one-for-one demand relationship.
The Brazil Comex Stat NCM 2601 extraction is not preserved as a direct query/export artifact in the cited URL.
SimFer's project-completion and shipment figures are company disclosures, not independent operating audits.
The ECB credit-risk discussion is qualitative; the pending sidecar states that no comparable same-day global credit-spread series was available by cutoff.
The IEA and Reuters support the conflict-related energy and shipping risk, but the report correctly does not assign responsibility for every individual maritime incident.
The latest public build remains blocked by the unrelated MT-GM-2026-11-18 revision-5 self-reference; this does not establish a defect in the candidate.
